info.name: Inventory · SPI Put-away Scan (handheld)
info.description:
The handheld put-away flow in the order the device walks it: session → scan box → scan zone/rack/shelf → confirm → complete.

AUTH — these routes carry NO user session.
The floor does not log in per carton, so the credential installed at enrolment IS the credential, and the person who logged in to enrol authors every scan the device makes.
  · Production — the front door (Apache / proxy) verifies the client certificate and passes its CN, having stripped any client-sent copy. The device sends no token.
  · Testing / fallback — send `X-Scan-Device: <token>`.
The tenant (client_id / branch_id) is read off the DEVICE row, never off the request body.

LABEL FORMATS accepted by `scanned_value` — all three still exist on labels in the building:
  1. Signed sticker   CBC1|<tenant>|<TYPE>|<id>|<nonce>|<sig>    TYPE = BOX | SHELF | RACK | ZONE
  2. Short form       SH:41   RC:7   ZN:3
  3. Bare number      16                                          (oldest box stickers — box only)

Every scan writes an activity row, pass or fail. A refusal is the one thing the log exists to remember.

Throttle: 120 requests / minute — a put-away is several calls and a bad scan is retried immediately by someone standing at a rack.

item.name: 01 · Session — who is this handheld, and what is open

exec: console.log('no open tasks for this device\u2019s client');

header.description: Omit when the client certificate is presented.

request.description:
The FIRST call the page makes. A device that is not enrolled, suspended or retired is told so here rather than halfway through a put-away.

RETURNS
  data.device              the enrolled handheld
  data.open[]              up to 50 open tasks, oldest issued first
      id, task_code
      box_code, spi_code
      step, step_label      where that task stands now
      destination           the full address in words
  data.count

401 rejected_unauthorized_device — not enrolled, or the token / certificate did not match.

The server decides what the barcode WAS and whether it belongs here. The handheld is never trusted to know which step it is on — it posts what the imager read, nothing more.

BODY
  scanned_value     required — the box label, in any accepted shape
  task_id           optional — omit on the first box scan; the server finds the task from the box
  staged_location   optional int — a location scanned BEFORE the box (see 03b)
  staged_kind       optional — shelf | zone | rack. Re-proved server-side; it is a client value.

RETURNS the state payload — see request 06 for the full field list.

REFUSALS (status:false + code)
  box_not_packed        the box resolves to no supplier invoice
  device_wrong_client   the box belongs to another tenant
  device_wrong_branch   another branch of the same tenant
  already_placed        a put-away already exists for this box

item.name: 03a · Scan — SHELF (ticks zone + rack + shelf at once)

exec: if (b.data && b.data.location) { console.log('already in this slot:', (b.data.location.boxes || []).length, 'box(es)'); }

request.description:
Scanning the SHELF satisfies the whole address — task.chain comes back with zone, rack and shelf all ticked in one go. Scan the zone or rack instead (03c) when the operator walks the chain down level by level.

The reply also carries what is ALREADY in that slot, so the screen can warn before the carton goes down:
  location.name
  location.boxes[]        box_code, spi_code, placed_at
  location.occupancy_pct

REFUSAL
  'No <kind> on this account matches that label' — the id is real but belongs to another tenant, or does not exist.

Real floors scan the shelf first and the carton second. The page HOLDS that location and hands it back with the box scan as staged_location + staged_kind.

The server re-proves both — they are client values and are never trusted as sent.

item.name: 03c · Scan — ZONE or RACK (walking the chain down)

request.description: task.next_level says which level the server wants next; task.chain shows how far down the operator has got. Swap {{zone_value}} for {{rack_value}} for the rack step.

item.name: 04 · Confirm — the operator agrees with what is on screen

request.description:
BODY
  slot    required — box | shelf | zone

Stamps box_confirmed_at / shelf_confirmed_at. Kept separate from the scan so the screen can show the carton's contents and have the operator agree before anything is committed.

Returns the same state payload.
Only passes once task.ready_to_complete is true. Writes the p2p_spi_putaways row carrying the location, the device serial, and the enrolling user as author.

item.name: 06 · Show — state for a page refresh

request.description:
Read-only, so a FINISHED task may be looked at — only the calls that WRITE require it to still be open.

If the task sat idle past inventory.scan_stale_minutes (5), the half-walked scans are dropped and the reply carries:
  stale_reset: true
  notice: 'That put-away was left too long — scan the box again to restart it.'

=== STATE PAYLOAD — returned by 02, 03, 04, 05 and 06 ===

data.device                  the enrolled handheld

data.task
  id, task_code, status
  step, step_label           where the operator is, in words
  expected                   what the server wants scanned next
  location_slot              which level this task is addressed to
  chain[]                    kind, id, name — zone → rack → shelf, each ticked or not
  next_level                 the level still owed
  required_scans, completed_scans
  fail_count, attempts_left
  box_scan_at, box_confirmed_at
  shelf_scan_at, shelf_confirmed_at
  ready_to_complete
  last_activity_at           the idle clock
  idle_after_minutes         5, from config — the page owns no threshold of its own
  idle_seconds_left          a DURATION, not a deadline: a handheld's clock is not trusted
  issued_at, expires_at

data.box
  id, box_code
  putaway_code               PUT-<box_code>
  spi_code
  scenario, scenario_label   s1 = 1 product → 1 box | s2 = 1 product → many boxes | s3 = many products → 1 box
  condition, is_stackable
  length_cm, width_cm, height_cm, dimensions_cm
  weight_kg, net_weight_kg, gross_weight_kg
  vol_weight_kg              L × W × H ÷ 5000 — a light, bulky carton is charged on this
  temp_min_c, temp_max_c
  flags[]                    handling warnings
  products[]                 what is inside the carton

data.destination
  full                       the address in words
  warehouse, zone, rack, shelf          codes
  zone_id, rack_id, shelf_id            ids
